title: Canonical integral scalar cokernel towers and their functoriality
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $A$ and chosen uniformizer $\varpi$, and any scheme $X$. Use the continuous integral coefficient ring sheaf $A_X$ and scalar multiplication maps supplied by [def-per-integral-lisse-reduction-data], in the category $\operatorname{Mod}(A_X)$ of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every $A_X$-module sheaf $M$ and $n\in\mathbf N$, define $Q_n(M)=\operatorname{coker}(\varpi^{n+1}:M\to M)$, with cokernel projection $\pi_{M,n}:M\to Q_n(M)$. Define $t_{M,n}:Q_{n+1}(M)\to Q_n(M)$ as the map induced by the identity on $M$, characterized by $t_{M,n}\circ\pi_{M,n+1}=\pi_{M,n}$. Define the inverse tower $Q(M):\mathbf N^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Mod}(A_X)$ by these objects and adjacent maps; all other transitions are their composites and the identity transitions are identities. For a module morphism $f:M\to N$, define $Q(f):Q(M)\to Q(N)$ by the cokernel-induced maps $Q_n(f)$ characterized by $\pi_{N,n}\circ f=Q_n(f)\circ\pi_{M,n}$. Define the functor $Q:\operatorname{Mod}(A_X)\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(A_X))$ with these object and morphism assignments. No local freeness, connectedness, nonempty-base or positive-rank assumption is imposed. This defines actual cokernels and maps, without asserting the additional quotient property of the adjacent transitions.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1), p.59: the functor M to (M/varpi^n M)_n, with its canonical quotient transitions and induced action on module maps; its scalar-cokernel construction on the ambient module category.
